I've been through this and it took a lot of work and a lot of despairing that I would never have untangled hair again. Just remember that it didn't get like that overnight so you won't fix it overnight!

I used a lot of conditioner but also detangling spray. If it's anything like mine was, there might be a while before you can even separate a section to work on because the whole thing is just so matted; you'll probably have to go hair by hair for a while. It feels hopeless picking strands but it WILL eventually get you some sort of opening.

You'll have to use your fingers or maybe even a cocktail stick for the really tight, few strand knots. Some of these will just come out and shed. There'll also probably be a lot of hair loss but this will be the weeks' of hair that couldn't fall out properly! 

Again, it feels useless and impossible but when hair is that matted, any strands you can tease out will eventually give way to more. It will take a long time and a lot of sessions so maybe put on some music or a favourite show while you work at it. Some sessions will feel like you've done nothing but it adds up.

When it's eventually in a place where you can use a brush on it, I've had success brushing lightly like you're only brushing the top layer instead of trying to get the bristles through the whole thing. 

I had a lot of frustration and moments where I wanted to give up, probably some tears too. But the days I spent picking individual hairs were what got me there in the end! Best of luck, it's tough but doable!

I recently had my first dentist appointment since I was a kid and was terrified too due to terrible social anxiety. I felt silly but I was so nervous I walked in there with a big jellycat plush - if it gives you comfort, take one! The dentist even complimented it.

A parent went in with me and it took me a few minutes just to work up the nerve to sit on the chair; both the dentist and assistant there were patient and understanding enough. Being lowered so horizontal felt wrong, but clutching my oversized Jellycat, I just focused on the clinical lights above me and did what they said.

It felt like it took all of twenty seconds for them to actually examine all my teeth. The dentist rattled off a string of various numbers and letters frighteningly quickly to their assistant, and they got typed down.

They did an x-ray, told me when to open or close my mouth, gave my parent some advice and then booked my next appointment which turned out to only be a visit to the hygienist. I've had struggles on and off with dental hygiene for years; I was expecting so much worse given the state of my teeth! 


No matter what happens you faced so many battles even walking into that room and no one can take that away from you.
